Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack Suffice to say that I have a medical condition that requires me to not get too hot. Bad things happen and they are very obvious, and not in my head. I can die if I get overheated. I just have to live with it. I also live and often work outside in one of the hottest and most humid parts of the country. Oh, and I'm not rich so I can't just hire people to do my bidding and stay inside all day. The clash of these issues has caused me to try numerous gadgets to stay cool and, honestly, this one works the best (and is one of the cheapest though it could be cheaper).

Chilling vests are ridiculously expensive and marginally effective.

"Snap towels" are a joke. Don't waste your money.

You need something with ice in it, people. And the plastic ice cubes don't work, either, and here's why: real ice melts and makes your shirt cool, too, and lasts LONGER, and is cheap.

So far this towel has worked great. I've used it a dozen times or so in very harsh conditions and bought another as a backup. You buy two dollars worth of bag ice, put it in a cooler, and you have at least two days of continuous personal cooling. The towel is long enough to fit around my big neck.

My niece tried it and told her dad she's never mowing the yard again without one. My daughter has never mowed the yard so I'm still astonished about that on two levels.

So tskile it from someone whose life and vision actually depends on staying cool (I know, sounds crazy, but it is true) : if you live in a HUMID area, this is the best balance of price and cooling you can get.

I am so serious about this product I left without it on me day and drive twenty miles back to get it, then twenty miles back to where I realized I'd forgotten it. Now that's a testimony.
text_fidelity_b: Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack

text_fidelity_a:
LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out I already had a Bowflex adjustable kettlebell that I liked a lot (though it's not perfect), but I wanted another adjustable kettlebell with lower weights for certain types of work. After four months of regular use, it's still in good shape and I'm glad I bought it.

Changing the plates is not as fast as on the Bowflex model, but it's easy, although the sliding tab sticks now and then. Still, it's fast enough for me to continue through a circuit without losing momentum, and that's what's important to me.

All the plates weight 2.5 lbs, and you can remove them however you like. That is, you don't have to take them from the top or the bottom. You will have to slot them back into the same place they came from, however, because they all curve in a certain way to give the kettlebell it's shape. The reviewer who mentioned sharp edges makes a good point, one worth considering for different exercises. For example, for swings it makes no difference to me where I pull the plates from, but if I'm doing shoulder presses, I pull them from the bottom or else I'll get my forearm unpleasantly poked and scraped as I use it. For a bottoms up carry, I find keeping the plates loaded at the top makes the weight more stable as I walk.

The plates make a slight rattle when swung -- that doesn't bother me, but it's something to keep in mind if working out within earshot of someone who might be disturbed by the noise. The plates do feel secure within the bell, but I still make it a habit to swing it so that the plates would fly away from me rather than at me if they came loose, and I swing them toward a wall or some other area where the plate wouldn't damage anyone. All that said, I'm sure I'm being overly cautious.

One thing I really like about this is the overall shape and footprint as compared to the Bowflex adjustable kettlebell. This one is a standard kettlebell size -- that makes it easier for me to handle, especially when it's in close to my body. The Bowflex is much larger, and that makes certain moves really awkward. It's not fair to compare these, though, given that they have very different weight ranges, but it's something I noticed. In those few places where the weights overlap, I almost always reach for this kettlebell over the Bowflex.

When buying exercise equipment, I'd much rather go to a shop where I can try it out in person and comparison shop. The pandemic made that impossible, so I crossed my fingers and hoped for the best. And it worked out. Even with its flaws, I've definitely gotten my money's worth for this.
text_fidelity_b: LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out

text_fidelity_a:
The Wornick Company MRE 1 case of HDR U.S. Military Surplus Humanitarian Meals Ready to Eat, FEMA 10 pack/ 20 Firstly, all of mine were well within their expiration date and I got 2 of all meals 1-5. For your home emergency kit, these are a great budget option. They were all completely fresh and nothing was stale or poorly packaged.

They're all also vegetarian, but I found the mains to still be super satisfying.

Personally I think they're such a ridiculously good value that I find myself eating one every week or two, spread across the week.

They are very spartan - a tiny bit more than they need to be, IMO. I'd have paid an extra $0.50-$1.00 for them to include a coffee and tea bag (they come with sugar but no beverage) as well as one more package of vegetable crackers or just all that instead of a cookie, since all the mains pair insanely well with the vegetable crackers. The matches work, but suck (but that hardly matters, we aren't living in refugee camps) and the spoon is of good quality, it comes with black pepper and red chili flakes (both of which are very welcome)

The variety is also pretty wanting and very over-heavy on the sweets, which is disappointing since the savory components are genuinely phenomenal - every one came with two unfrosted actual brand-name brown sugar/cinnamon pop tarts (my favorite, so no complaints there) as well as a shortbread cookie, oatmeal cookie, peanut butter and strawberry jam. The savory components are all vegetarian, with two retort pouches and a package of vegetable crackers.

As for the food taste itself, I'll start with the weak points. I don't have a huge sweet tooth, so I was a little disappointed in that part. The poptarts are exactly what you'd expect - Brown sugar/cinnamon is the only flavor I like, so that's great. The oatmeal cookie is very dry and dense but satisfying, not too sweet and the peanut butter helps it a lot. I was a lot less keen on the shortbread cookie, which was also very dry, dense, and not to my taste. It is palatable with the strawberry jam to take up some of the dryness, but it's not satisfying to me at all. The peanut butter and jam themselves are quite good.

Now for the strengths. The savory parts are the real standout. They're all vegetarian, and the portions seem small, but I'm not out fighting a war, so they work out to be absolutely perfect portions. I just had the vegetable barley stew with some triscuits and the oatmeal cookie + peanut butter for dinner since my wife's not home this evening, and I'm super full.

There are only a few different mains too, rice and vegetables, vegetable barley stew, "peas" and tomatoes (Black eye peas), etc. And they are all generally same-y, but with some of the crushed pepper, they've all got a lovely flavor and very satiating. They also all somehow make great dips for tortilla chips or crackers.

And the star of the HDR is the vegetable crackers. I genuinely wish I could buy those things by the case, they're straight up fantastic on their own - not dry, not stale, not bland, but they really elevate the mains with some crunch and more savory flavors. Seriously, I wish I knew where to buy them on their own, I'd never buy chips, saltines or triscuits again. The only downside is that you only get one pack per HDR and both rations really need them, so I wind up supplementing them with a tortilla or aforementioned triscuits.

I didn't notice them being "gassy" like another reviewer mentioned. I like meat, but I think that person might just need more fiber in their daily diet.

I find myself using about one a week on its own, bringing a little collapsible silicone bowl for microwaving the mains and a baggie of crackers or tortilla chips to supplement the vegetable crackers. I'll eat the poptarts if I don't have time to make breakfast, I'll have the cookies if I'm in the university library and studying, and I'll have a main for lunch a couple times a week. I carry my own hot-sauce, so a little of that also livens up the mains. The only way they could be better for this is if the shortbread cookie was replaced with a granola bar or another pack of those crackers (two big cookies a day is just too much), include some kind of beverage like instant coffee and/or tea, and if there was some way to (and this is truly a first world problem) make the retort pouches microwave-safe.

Oh, and the bags they come in are super sturdy and tolerate being knocked around like a champ.

So overall, for under $5 for an entire day's worth of calories, I'm seriously nitpicking. These are solid for camping, good to keep one or two in your car's emergency kit, and worth keeping a couple cases at home for your disaster kit. I find them a great way to have portion control for the occasional meal throughout the week, too. They were a godsend when I worked in the field as a paramedic and sometimes went an entire 12-24hrs without seeing my station.

Seriously though. It's an entire day's worth of pretty wholesome food for $5. The fact that it's edible at all is kind of insane.
text_fidelity_b: The Wornick Company MRE 1 case of HDR U.S. Military Surplus Humanitarian Meals Ready to Eat, FEMA 10 pack/ 20

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Protocol 2.7 Mens and Womens Mountain Bike, 27.5-Inch Wheels, 21-Speed Drivetrain, Lightweight Aluminum Frame, Full Suspension, Matte Blue This is a nice bike and a much better quality than the average old bike out there. It has a few faults, but overall, my husband and I have been pleased with it.

I'm partial to the color blue, so I think it's absolutely gorgeous with its color. It rides well. My husband and I ride on a little trail behind our house. There are lots of curves and bumps and ups and downs with hills and it does well with them. That said, the seat is the worst that I've ever ridden on. It is awful! I know the average bike seat is uncomfortable, but this one is most definitely so. It left me incredibly bruised the first time I rode it. I've mostly adjusted to it now and know when to raise myself off the seat to avoid more bruising, but it took some time. If you don't like skinny and hard bike seats, prepare to swap this one out.

It's also sometimes hard to swap gears. When I'm moving up a gear, it's like it doesn't fully swap over and I hear clicking. I have to move back down a gear and try again. This happens pretty often, though not every time. My husband has the same complaint. The kickstand isn't the best, either. This one simply won't hold the bike up on its own. I have to prop it up on something else to keep it from falling. We have a couple of cheaper bikes that we're able to keep up with just the kickstand.

There is some assembly required, which is a negative to ordering online. My husband did all the assembly work, but didn't have any trouble. This does take time, though, and is most definitely something to consider when ordering. (In stores, most bikes are already put together for you, without an extra fee...if in store is an option for you.)

Despite a few faults, we've been happy with this bike, overall.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Protocol 2.7 Mens and Womens Mountain Bike, 27.5-Inch Wheels, 21-Speed Drivetrain, Lightweight Aluminum Frame, Full Suspension, Matte Blue

text_fidelity_a: BETIMESYU Fitness Tracker Color Screen Waterproof Activity Tracker Smart Watch Remote Photography Heart Rate Blood Pressure Blood Oxygen Monitor Step Calorie Counter Pedometer for Women Men Kids This product does not measure oxygen accurately and, therefore, can be dangerous to people with low oxygen. This could potentially be dangerous to a person with low oxygen who believes the false measurement is accurate and then overexerts himself/herself.

Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue) A bit of a conumdrum here with two ways to look at it. I am 6'3" and currently weigh 225 Lbs. Not a lightweight but as my Pulmonologist informs me "you're no longer clinically obese, you're just obese". Thanks Doc! A left-handed compliment if I ever heard one.

And there lies the rub. The first time I shook this out I had mild difficulty in getting the tabs and latches to hook up-- like I did just now. That seems to inspire a little less confidence in how safely it will support me without crashing down. Once it is expanded and set up it appears to be pretty sturdy. The color also makes it easy to see in the yard.

But having just had double knee replacement I was a bit concerned that it would hold me without making me faceplant in the yard. When I asked my wife to watch me sit on it in the kitchen she said "don't do that!". The sight of me pulling it out and clicking it together didn't inspire confidence in her either.

It did hold me while sitting still although I was a bit reluctant to shift my weight around on it. That would be my major sticking point. On a yard that is not completely level I know that I would have to be careful. The other part of that is that leaning forward or to one side suddenly puts additional stress on whichever part of the base is sitting on the ground. I am not convinced that leaning over wouldn't cause the stool to buckle and me to fall over.

So there it is. It seems to be a smart design and should solve the problem of having a stool available when needed. However plastic is not indestructible and will often bend as it is stressed over and over again. Good idea, decent execution, but it doesn't inspire any confidence for someone my size.
text_fidelity_b: Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue)

LUMINTOP C01 USB Rechargeable Bicycle Front Light, IP68 Waterproof, Bike Headlight with Super Bright Cree Neutral LED, Road Cycling Safety Flashlight, Easy Install & Quick Release This bike light should be getting a 5 star, but because on the first charge the small cover piece to the input for the charge broke off, we have to drop it to a 4. My wife has been using such tiny charing ports for years (like us all) and she’s very careful. This thing easily popped off and in spite of her dainty skills at repairing such tiny things, cannot get it back on. That’s a minus for us.

But as a tool, it’s great. So if they can fix that flaw in how the port cover is attached, we’d be happy to give it a 5.

It arrived in a nice box (for yourself or a gift) in 3 parts: light, clamp, and charger. She charged right away - after as she pushed the piece in it popped off - and we put it on. She severely broke her foot a couple weeks ago and gets around for the next 3 months on a scooter. But she wants to be able to see at night if she’s moving through the house, or if we are outside, so we thought a bike light might work. It’s perfect for that. It fits on the handles of her scooter as easily as a bike - and we plan on switching it to a bike when she’s recovered. In the mean time, the 3 levels of light mean she can see safely in the house without being disruptive, and she can see safely outside moving to the car or around our home. It’s really easy to clamp and remove - she takes it off when we are in the car so it won’t get broken off. And she can easily pop it back on.

Overall this is a great light and minus the flaw with the port cover, we are really happy with it. That we cannot overlook, however, because there is little doubt that in 12+ weeks on the scooter and future use on the bike, covering the port hole would be a safety issue (rain). So the 4 star has to stay. Happy to have it though.

text_fidelity_a:
Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel, 20-Pound Max Drag I'm loving this reel. It replaced an Ambassadeur 5500C. The differences are pretty obvious. The Patriarch includes both a friction and magnetic breaking system. This might be a good thing if you have experience but it does take some time to get used to it. Nearest I can figure, the magnetic breaking is most effective at the beginning of the case where the speed is highest while the mechanical brake operates across the whole cast. When I change lures I usually turn up the magnetic to 8-10 and then adjust the mechanical until I clean casts. Then I back off the magnetic for the same result. The end result is nice long casts with fewer rats nests. Then - to add to the complication - you can pop off the side and adjust how many magnets are active in the magnetic breaking. I keep two on and four off (must be done in pairs). I get a few more yards (5 to 10 maybe) from the Patriarch compared with the 5500c.

Reeling back in is smooth. The moving eye lays the line smoothly on the spool but I notice that during casting the eye stays in one place. I can't remember for sure but I thought the 5500c eye moved during casts. Careful when you release the spool. The tension on the line may be enough to get the spools spinning and you can end up with a rats nest without even casting.

The Patriarch fits nicely in the palm while on the rod. It allows me to keep a finger on the spool and keep in touch with the line out the front. I have it mated to a St. Croix Legend Tournament Bass Casting Rod and I think the combination is perfect though I'd like to try it out with a slightly lighter and slower action rod. I'll bet it can shoot a 1/2 ounce lure a half mile!

I didn't like my dealings with support. As I mentioned, you can engage or disengage magnets in the break system but I couldn't figure out how. The minimal instruction pamphlet didn't give any clues and neither did their support website. In fact, looking through some forums I'm guessing most people find access to the magnets obvious. But I didn't know how to do it and support responded with "Unfortunately, to experiment with the centrifugal breaks, you must take
the reel apart to access them." Wow. Helpful guys. Maybe I lost something in the translation. I don't know. Fortunately for me I feel the reel is so well built I'll never have to contact support so I'll just ignore them.

You can fish well with any nice baitcaster. This isn't going to put bigger or more fish on your hook. But you'll find each cast is a pleasure.
text_fidelity_b: Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel, 20-Pound Max Drag

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver Easy to setup and adjust, feels sturdy and secure. It really would take a bit of effort to remove a bike from it if you have it locked down.

Seems like a really good value.

There were a few stumbling blocks I encountered, though. First, the locking hitch pin that Sawgman sells is a bit expensive, compared to other locking pins you can find. However, because the rack had a threaded hole, a standard 1/2” pin won’t fit through. I ended up just yawing the supplied pin, and used a small Master Lock with a small enough shackle diameter to fit. Probably not as secure as the proprietary locking pin, but it should be enough to dissuade anyone looking for a quick grab and go.

Speaking of shackle diameter, it was a bit of a challenge to find the perfect locks to use on the bars. Your typical MasterLock is about 7mm, which is too big; and 5mm was small enough that you could still pull the trigger and move the bar up with ease. In the end I found the MasterLock 141T set of two locks (Keyed alike) with a 6mm shackle was the best fit. The shackle is just small enough to fit through the hole, but thick enough to keep the trigger secure.

So the TLDR, but a lock with a 6mm diameter shackle to secure your bikes.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver

Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black) NGL, it's a slick looking knife, but it isn't well constructed.

The blade looks good and the scales feel good in the hand. The blade definitely is sharp. The issue is the pivot point of the knife and the scales around the pivot point.

You'll notice that there is a nice index finger groove up near the pivot point. This is a nice ergo component, however when gripping the knife here the scales flex and cause a severe amount of blade play at the pivot point. Inversely, grabbing the blade towards the base and wigging it will cause the scales at that finger well to flex.

As much as I would like to write this off as a 1-off construction issue, I had an unrelated individual talk about the very same issue they had with this knife. They had sourced the knife from their local B&M and had mentioned the issue. I told them I had one in the mail and would check it when the knife showed up. Sure enough 2 instances of this knife with the same issue.

So buyer beware. I have heard good things about this knife maker and this knife so I decided to test the waters with this blade. I will be sending this knife back and I doubt I will be buying another Eafengrow even if it's another G-10 D2 for sub $20.
text_fidelity_b: Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count Brand new out of the box, trying to set it up, and this thing is already presenting challenges. If you're thinking of getting one here's what you need to know: the charger is magnet so it attracts the charging prongs to the device easily HOWEVER, the magnet isn't strong enough to hold onto the device. If you set it down, it pops off the charging cord. You have to lay it down, propped on something, veeeerrrrrry carefully. I haven't even worn this thing and I can see that this is going to drive me nuts!!! I may deploy some high tech hacks - like a twist tie or some masking tape - to content with the charger design. :-p I'll come back and write more once I've set up and worn this thing.

You should know, I"m a devoted fitbit user and wear my devices out - they retire off to wherever beloved exhausted devices go after their life ends. I'm so sad my Alta HR died. I want it back! I still have my old Flex as a backup. I've never considered buying another brand of tracker and probably never will.

2/8/2020 - I'm back and I've upgraded stars from 3 to 5. The magnetic charger thing is still a bummer but absolutely everything else about this tracker is phenomenal. I can't believe this thing has so many features at its price point. Interaction with the screen is intuitive. The features available on-screen are a step up from the Alta HR. There's a Breath/relax/meditation function, a Timer, you can view and enable/disable the silent alarm settings right on the device, you can see how many steps you have left to meet the Reminder To Move target. I simply ADORE this thing!!! Fitbit, you really brought it with this tracker. I thank you.

7/7/2020 Back again with more information. Exactly 6 months after purchase, the device won't sync so I tried pairing it again to Bluetooth. The device won't pair so I tried resetting it per Fitbit product help web pages. The device won't reset. Now what? I loved the features on this device but it's hard to love something that won't work. Back to 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count

text_fidelity_a: OCOOPA Rechargeable Hand Warmers, 10000mAH Electric Handwarmer Winter Warm 15 Hours Portable Hands Heater for Men Women When I was a kid my dad used to hand me his hand warmer when we were outside during cold weather.  It was a "manual" kind - the interior had something like rock wool that was soaked in butane and lit and then the metal casing was slid inside a thick insulated bag and put in your pocket.  It could get rather hot!  I mention this because it brings back fond memories, but also to illustrate the difference in the "old fashioned" hand warmers and this one.  I love how easy this is to charge, even in my car, and the 3 levels of warmth depending on how cold it is and/or what you are doing.  I can put this in my pocket on low heat while I'm scraping the ice off my windshield and windows, then grab the warmer and let my fingers regain some feeling before trading the scraper for the shovel and shoveling the snow away from the car and off the sidewalk.  However many times I need to, I can stop shoveling and grab the warmer to keep my hands and fingers from going numb - that's what I appreciate having this handwarmer!  If you have kids that wait at the bus stop or have to walk to school even in winter, giving them a handwarmer might be just the thing to give them a "boost" of warmth while standing in the cold!

text_fidelity_a:
Onos Trading Company Carabelle Polarized Sunglasses (+2.50 Add Power), Black, Grey Lens, One Size The perfect sunglasses. I've bought I lot of sunglasses, quite a few with integrated readers. These are about the most expensive, and yet the msot worth-it.

The frame fits perfectly. (This is the Carabelle, for medium/large heads. If you have a tiny head, the Lagoon will probably fit better.) The lens quality is very good. I've had mine quite a while and they haven't gotten scratched, but I don't put them in a pocket unprotected as some other reviewers have done. And they 're dark enough, with a good reading area.

The one thing to know is, darkness. The grey is the "dark" lens, amber is the "less dark." Blue is grey+mirror (so a bit darker, better for cutting glare), green is amber+mirror (less dark than blue.)

The reading area is visible from outside the glasses. It won't be in your way, but others can notice it. Which has been a positive conversation piece for us, such as on a cruise when other travelers notice and are suddenly jealous.

I started to send it back but decided to see how well a fan like this actually works when charged.  I knew I was not going to use it in a tent or at least not for everyone since the tent is divided by little velcro screens.  I plan on buying a larger fan for the tents. Most of the other fans I saw are rechargeable by getting rechargeable double A or triple A batteries. I don't want another device laying around the house on a table that is used just to recharge batteries for a fan. I wanted to be able to plug it into any computer, or a USB port on a docking station or use any of the two powerbanks I have.  We carry the power banks with us when we go away. I bought the tent for the back yard for the kids but I am sure we will use if we decide to travel with the tent.  My ultimate goal is to get a solar panel or panels and some how mount them near the tent so the sun can recharge our powerbanks all day. Almost forgot, I decided to keep this thing right above my monitors.  I only need it on setting 1 or 2 and I am cool.  It has 3 settings and the third one is very good.  See the photo of the light as well. It is built inside of the fan itself.

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick I've previously owned a Klymit V without the "Luxe," but a piece of the one valve it had broke off in short order. This Klymit V Luxe has valves which *appear* to me to have fewer fiddly parts, and there are two of them--more on why that's good in a moment!

First off, these pads have a smart design. Although there is no railing per say, the Vs help to keep you on them which is good news if you do not stay in one place on a bed. The material keeps the air inside from feeling cold (and presumably from drinking in too much of the earth's cold).

The primary use I gave my original V was as a buffer between me and an extremely ill-suited new mattress while I desperately shopped for solutions. And although I've been a backpacker in the past, sadly, my primary intended use for the Static V Luxe is to act as a buffering layer when I need to sleep on other people's mattresses. I have considerable back health issues, and this padding is incredibly helpful for when I cannot be on my own mattress. I purchased this size this time because the original V is so much smaller than a twin bed that it was downright silly trying to use it for my purpose. Also I use a body pillow and change positions a lot. This will clearly be nicer for managing nights out of my own bed.

Now I saw someone complaining about the two valves because they are confusing. This person has probably never experienced the downsides of only having one valve for letting air out of a mattress. Sure, you need to be certain that the valve you are not blowing into is closed so that the mattress can properly inflate, but oh, my word, it is soooooo much easier to get the air out of this mattress pad! I could almost never get my original V small enough to properly stick into its dry sack. But this larger V luxe easily packs up smaller than I could get the original V to go. Ok, so maybe "easy" is relative. You do need to open both valves, roll it down from bottom to top, open it up again, fold a few times, and roll once more to get it maximally small. But it actually works and stuffs in the drysack.

I hope if you're reading this that you have more adventurous uses afoot, but I do recommend this Static V Luxe and wish I'd had one back when I was a backpacker!
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick

text_fidelity_a:
MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag This tent seems like a great value at first. But when you can't sleep because of water seeping in, then drive yourself mad trying to tear down the tent in the morning you'll regret not buying a real tent.

The only plus I can give to this tent is that it sets up super easily. But to be honest, it's not really that much better than just setting up any other tent. The mechanism they have to pop the tent open works. But you're adding a lot of weight and mechanical complexity to something that's not very difficult in the first place.

On to the negatives.

It's impossibly annoying to tear down. While the tent pops open easily, it's a total pain to close. All of the plastic arms will start popping out of the mechanism. There's 8 joints you need to pull and close, one by one. And then you have to figure out which way the thing actually closes. But there's so much tension in the arms attached to the central hub that if you don't do it just right everything starts popping out.

So instead of just popping your tent poles out of the ground and pulling them out of the tent, you have to tear apart and rebuild this complicated lever mechanism spring loaded hub thing in the middle of the woods. And that's after you got no sleep because there's water in your tent.

The rain fly doesn't cover nearly enough of the tent. So if there's any rain it will rain directly on the tent, where as I said above, water will start seeping through into the tent. not just a little dampness. We had actual puddles in the tent.

I've had $20 Walmart tents that did a better job than this thing. It's not worth the money. It's overly complicated. And worst of all it just doesn't provide adequate shelter.
text_fidelity_b: MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag

Our trip took us down to CA from WA and we needed something that would do the trick as an "assistant" to our little fridge in the camper.

I spent a lot of time eyeballing these in town and online. When I saw the price The Wonderful World of Amazonia(tm) was charging for it and read many of the reviews I was sold.

This cooler did what we needed to do. We camped at that one place for four days. I loaded it up with ice ONCE and kept it outside under the shade of the bedends. I won't say there was 100% of the ice remaining, because there wasn't. What there was remaining was enough ice to keep the melted water cool to keep the items in the cooler cool.

For what it's worth, I'm a retired chef. I know all about HACCP. I know what needs to be refrigerated for how long and at what temperature. I wasn't worried about this cooler and my food in it.

text_fidelity_a:
Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft I have zero business affiliation with amazon or Shrade. I just like to help people make a decision on purchasing affordable gear. Many times I have bought less expensive gear and was sorry I did. However this won’t be the case with Schrade. If you are just getting into camping/bushcraft start with this knife. I bought my knives directly from the Schrade website (shut down now) about 2-3 years ago. I have 3 of their knives Sch37, Sch57, and Schf52; and was only out of about $60 for all 3. They are great knives for a beginner. Yes, they have some issues. But they may not bother everyone.

The Bad: The basic handles are not the most comfortable over long periods of use. Later, get the micarta scales the basic scales are not comfortable when chopping or don’t chop.

The chimpping on top is a bit aggressive when not wearing gloves and doing percussive tasks.

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft

text_fidelity_a:
Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black This is a very well made tac light, very bright and compact. It uses a lithium battery which means it can sit around for years and still be ready when you need it. I like it, but there are a couple things to be aware of, especially for a tactical light, which means something that has to be 100% reliable and ready when you need it.

1) Hitting the mode you want is very tricky. You have to hit the switch just the right number of times (of course) and most tricky at just the right interval. The timing is VERY fast and it is different if you are going to use a particular mode temporarily (light press and hold button) or switching to that mode (press firmly and release staying on that mode). It takes practice, lots of it to hit the mode you want reliably.

2) When the battery runs out, there is absolutely NO WARNING. Either you will click it on and nothing happens or (most of the time) you will click it on and in a few seconds it goes dead. NOT a good situation for a tactical light. The only way this light can be absolutely ready for a critical situation is to put a new fresh $4 battery in it. Battery life isn't great, but that's the price for such a bright light running on a single CR123 battery. Just hope it is ready when you need it. A low battery indicator would be nice.

Still I gave it a soft 4 stars, maybe 3.5 would be more precise. It is a good light if you use it often enough to be good at hitting the right mode and if you have a fresh battery in it.
text_fidelity_b: Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black
